questions.q: A company wants to move 200 on-premises virtual machines to AWS as they are, using continuous block-level replication to keep cutover downtime minimal. Which service should it use?
questions.hint: A rehost tool that works on whole servers.
questions.explanation: Application Migration Service (MGN) replicates source servers continuously and launches them on AWS with minimal cutover downtime. DataSync transfers files and objects, not whole running servers.

questions.q: A mainframe-dependent application was recently upgraded on-premises, and the business decides not to migrate it for at least two years. Which migration strategy is this?
questions.hint: Keep it where it is, for now.
questions.explanation: Retain (revisit) means keeping an application in its current environment until migrating makes sense. Retire would mean decommissioning it, but this application is still needed.

questions.q: Which AWS CAF perspective helps ensure that cloud investments accelerate the company's digital transformation goals and business outcomes?
questions.explanation: The Business perspective connects cloud adoption to business strategy and outcomes, through capabilities such as strategy management, product management and data monetization. Governance handles oversight and risk.

questions.q: A company must continuously collect evidence of how its AWS resources comply with frameworks such as PCI DSS and GDPR in order to prepare for audits. Which service should it use?
questions.hint: Evidence about your own environment, collected automatically.
questions.explanation: Audit Manager continuously collects evidence from your AWS usage and maps it to compliance framework controls. Artifact only provides AWS's own compliance reports.

questions.q: Which TWO are recommended best practices for the AWS account root user? (Choose two.)
options: Use it for everyday administrative tasks
Share its credentials with team leads for emergencies
Rotate its password daily and email it to the team
Do not create access keys for it
questions.hint: Protect it strongly and use it as little as possible.
questions.explanation: Protect the root user with MFA, avoid creating root access keys, and use IAM or Identity Center identities for daily work. Sharing root credentials, in any form, breaks accountability.

questions.q: Administrators need interactive shell access to EC2 instances without opening inbound SSH port 22 or maintaining bastion hosts, and every session must be logged. Which service fits?
options: A bastion host with port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0
questions.explanation: Session Manager provides browser or CLI shell access through the SSM Agent, with no inbound ports or bastions needed, and sessions can be logged to S3 or CloudWatch. A bastion with SSH open to the world is exactly what you want to avoid.

questions.q: A company needs a MySQL-compatible relational database that keeps six copies of the data across three Availability Zones and grows storage automatically. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Aurora is MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible, replicates six copies of data across three AZs, and scales storage automatically. DynamoDB is NoSQL, not relational.

questions.q: The operations team wants to be notified whenever average CPU utilization on a production instance stays above 80% for 5 minutes. What should it configure?
options: An Amazon CloudWatch alarm that publishes to an SNS topic
questions.hint: Metrics, a threshold, and a notification.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch alarms watch a metric against a threshold over a period and can notify through SNS. CloudTrail logs API calls; it doesn't monitor performance metrics.

questions.q: A company wants to centrally define backup policies and automate backups of its EBS volumes, RDS databases, DynamoDB tables and EFS file systems. Which service fits?
questions.hint: One policy-based service for many resource types.
questions.explanation: AWS Backup centralizes and automates backups across AWS services through backup plans. Glacier Deep Archive is a storage class, not a tool for scheduling and managing backups.

questions.q: Which type of data transfer is generally free of charge on AWS?
options: Data transferred out to the internet
Data transferred in to AWS from the internet
Data transferred out through a NAT gateway
questions.explanation: Inbound data transfer from the internet is generally free. Data transferred out to the internet and between Regions is charged per GB, and a NAT gateway charges for the data it processes.
